title: Closest Point
statement:
Read a list of points, keep each one as a pair of coordinates, and find the point closest to the origin `(0, 0)`.

The first line of the input is a count `n` (at least 1). Each of the next `n` lines holds one point as two integers `x y`, each between -1000 and 1000. Print the closest point as `x y` on one line. A point's distance from the origin grows with `x * x + y * y`, so you can compare that value and skip square roots. When several points are equally close, print the one that comes first in the input.

Input:

```text
3
3 4
1 2
-2 -2
```

Expected output:

```text
1 2
```
hints: Store each point as one value that holds both coordinates, so a whole point moves around together.
Keep the best point so far and its distance. Replace it only when a new point is strictly closer, so ties keep the earlier one.
